54906.text: Which from following compounds does NOT contain phenolic -OH group?

Eugenol has one phenolic -OH group on its benzene ring. Gallic acid ( 3,4,5 -trihydroxybenzoic acid) contains three phenolic -OH groups. 73946.subject: General Ability
73946.text: Which one of the following about different frictional force is correct?
options: Kinetic fricition > Static friction > Rolling friction
Static friction Rolling fricition Kinetic fricition
Static friction Kinetic friction Rolling friction
Static friction Kinetic friction = Rolling friction
73946.sol: Static friction Kinetic friction Rolling friction - Static friction is the frictional force that prevents two surfaces from sliding past each other when they are not moving relative to each other. - Kinetic friction is the frictional force that opposes the relative motion of two surfaces sliding past each other. - Rolling friction is the frictional force that opposes the motion of a rolling object.

73952.subject: General Ability
73952.text: What is the coordination number of Na ⁺ and Cl ⁻ ions in NaCl lattice?
73952.sol: In the NaCl (sodium chloride) crystal lattice, each sodium ion ( Na ⁺ ) is surrounded by 6 chloride ions ( Cl ⁻ ), and each chloride ion is surrounded by 6 sodium ions. This arrangement is known as a face-centered cubic (FCC) structure, where each ion is in contact with 6 nearest neighbours in all directions. This high coordination number of 6 ensures strong electrostatic interactions between ions, contributing to the stability of the crystal lattice and the characteristic properties of NaCl .

84741.subject: Zoology
84741.text: Elbow joint is an example of
84741.sol: In hinge joint, the convex surface of one bone fits into the concave surface of another bone. eg, knee, elbow and interphalangeal joints. Pivot joint, one bone is fixed and second articulated, eg, atlas and axial of skull rotate with axis vertebra. Gliding joints primarily permit side-by-side and back-and-forth gliding movements, eg, intercarpal joints and intertarsal joints. Curve A: Reverse bias, Curve B: Unbiased

112789.sol: Pollutants that can be traced back to specific, identifiable sources of contamination are referred to as point source pollutants.

112910.subject: Chemistry
112910.text: Why was the use of DDT eventually banned in India?
options: It caused adverse effects on the environment and health
It was too expensive for widespread use
It led to the development of resistant pests
112910.sol: The use of DDT was banned in India due to its adverse effects on the environment and health.

113362.subject: Chemistry
113362.text: What type of alignment do domains in ferrimagnetic substances exhibit?

All domains have their magnetic moments aligned in anti-parallel directions.
Some domains have their magnetic moments aligned in parallel directions, while others have them aligned in ant
Domains do not have any alignment in ferrimagnetic substances.
113362.sol: Domains in ferrimagnetic substances exhibit some alignment in parallel directions and some alignment in anti-parallel directions.

113364.subject: Chemistry
113364.text: How is thermal energy spread throughout a metal when heat is supplied to one portion of it?
options: Thermal energy is absorbed by positive ions.
Thermal energy is uniformly spread throughout by free electrons.
Thermal energy is lost as light.
Thermal energy is transferred to neighboring metals.
113364.sol: When heat is supplied to one portion of a metal, thermal energy is uniformly spread throughout by free electrons, as stated in the paragraph.

114634.subject: Chemistry
114634.text: Who provided the physical justification and interpretation of the Arrhenius equation?
114634.sol: Swedish chemist Arrhenius provided the physical justification and interpretation of the Arrhenius equation.

114639.subject: Chemistry
114639.text: How are the units of rate defined in gaseous reactions when the concentration of gases is expressed in terms of their partial pressures?
114639.sol: In gaseous reactions, when the concentration of gases is expressed in terms of their partial pressures, the units of the rate equation are "atm s-1."

115356.subject: Chemistry
115356.text: What is meant by the term "Electrophoresis"?
options: The migration of charged colloidal particles under the influence of an electric field.
The settling of colloidal particles due to gravity.
The process of separating colloidal particles using a filter.
The diffusion of gas molecules through a semipermeable membrane.
115356.sol: Correct Option is : (A) The migration of charged colloidal particles under the influence of an electric field.

115731.subject: Chemistry
115731.text: Why are the trihalides of nitrogen exceptional?
options: Nitrogen has a small atomic size
Nitrogen can form strong hydrogen bonds
115731.sol: The exceptional behavior of nitrogen's trihalides is due to its unique electron configuration.

115892.subject: Chemistry
115892.text: What is the hybridization state of phosphorus in phosphorus trichloride (PCl 3 )?
115892.sol: The paragraph states that phosphorus in phosphorus trichloride has a pyramidal shape and is sp3 hybridized.

116596.subject: Chemistry
116596.text: Within which range of atomic numbers,is there a significant increase in the density of these elements?
116596.sol: A significant increase in density is noted from titanium (Z = 22) to copper (Z = 29).

116724.subject: Chemistry
116724.text: What is the color of Cu2+ when it is in the 3d9 state?
116724.sol: Cu2+ in the 3d9 state is blue.

116777.subject: Chemistry

116777.sol: The paragraph states that Zn2+ is colorless when it is in the 3d10 state.

options: They are responsible for the color of the complex
They balance the charge of the complex ion
117465.sol: Counter ions in a coordination compound balance the charge of the complex ion.

(A) is not correct but (R) is correct

On the other hand, K ₃[ Fe ( CN )₆] is a coordination complex that yields K ^+ and the complex ion [ Fe ( CN )₆]³⁻ . 117818.subject: Chemistry
117818.text: Which of the following complex is optically inactive?
options: [ RhCl ( CO ) ( PPh ₃ ) ( NH ₃ ) ]
117818.sol: [ RhCl ( CO ) ( PPh ₃ ) ( NH ₃ ) ] is optically inactive as it is square planar complex. It has plane of symmetry.

117822.subject: Chemistry
117822.text: Which of the following is a pair of diamagnetic complexes?
117822.sol: [ Co ( NH ₃ )₆ ]³⁺ and [ Fe ( CN )₆ ]⁴⁻ are diamagnetic complexes.

118092.subject: Chemistry
118092.text: Match the following: The correct answer is array lll A & B & C & D array
118092.sol: p-alkylhalide undergoes SN2 reaction with KOH in high dielectric medium like water and undergoes E ₂ reaction in less dielectric medium like alcohol. In acidic medium - OH group is protonated in order to form a better leaving group, H ₂ O .

118396.subject: Chemistry
118396.text: What is the main feature of oxidation reactions of alcohols?
options: Formation of a carbon-oxygen double bond
Formation of a carbon-carbon double bond
Formation of a carbon-carbon triple bond
118396.sol: Oxidation reactions of alcohols involve the formation of a carbon-oxygen double bond, typically in aldehydes or ketones.

118488.subject: Chemistry
118488.text: In hydroboration-oxidation, which carbon of the alkene does boron attach to?
options: The sp carbon with fewer hydrogen atoms
The sp2 carbon with fewer hydrogen atoms
The sp2 carbon with greater hydrogen atoms
The sp3 carbon with fewer hydrogen atoms
118488.sol: Boron attaches to the sp2 carbon with greater hydrogen atoms in hydroboration-oxidation.

118972.subject: Chemistry
118972.text: In which type of solvents, such as benzene, ether, methanol, and chloroform, are aldehydes and ketones generally fairly soluble?
118972.sol: Aldehydes and ketones are fairly soluble in organic solvents like benzene, ether, methanol, chloroform, etc.

119130.subject: Chemistry
119130.text: What are the number of individual atoms in the structure of 4-Fluoroacetophenone?
options: 8 Carbon, 1 Oxygen, 1 Fluorine and 9 Hydrogen atoms
8 Carbon, 1 Oxygen, 1 Fluorine and 7 Hydrogen atoms
8 Carbon, 1 Oxygen, 1 Fluorine and 6 Hydrogen atoms
8 Carbon, 2 Oxygen, 1 Fluorine and 7 Hydrogen atoms
119130.sol: Correct Option is : (B) 8 Carbon, 1 Oxygen, 1 Fluorine and 7 Hydrogen atoms

119352.subject: Chemistry
119352.text: The product formed in aldol condensation is:
options: a-beta hydroxy aldehyde or a betahydroxy ketone
119352.sol: Aldehydes and ketones having at least one -hydrogen atom in presence of dilute alkali give -hydroxy aldehyde or -hydroxy ketone. Caution Those aldehydes which does not have -hydrogen atom like HCHO , does not give aldol condensation reaction.

119813.subject: Chemistry
119813.text: An aromatic compound ‘A’ on treatment with aqueous ammonia and heating forms compound ‘B’ which on heating with Br 2 and KOH forms a compound ‘C’ of molecular formula C 6 H 7 N. What are the IUPAC names of compounds A, B and C?
options: A= Benzoic acid, B=Benzamide and C=Aniline
A= Aniline, B=Benzamide and C=Benzoic acid
A= Benzamide, B=Benzoic acid and C=Aniline
A= Benzoic acid, B=Aniline and C=Benzamide

119961.subject: Chemistry
119961.text: What is the most common mode of addition or chain growth polymerization?
options: Free radical governed addition or chain growth polymerization
119961.sol: The most common mode of addition or chain growth polymerization is free radical governed addition or chain growth polymerization.

120194.subject: Chemistry
120194.text: Besides sodium benzoate, what other salts are used as food preservatives?
120194.sol: Salts of sorbic acid and propanoic acid are also used as food preservatives.

120243.subject: Chemistry
120243.text: Where are the majority of receptors located in the cell?
120243.sol: The majority of receptors are embedded in the cell membrane.

120725.subject: Chemistry
120725.text: What is cellulose primarily composed of?
120725.sol: Cellulose is composed of beta-D-glucose units joined by glycosidic linkages.

120981.subject: Chemistry
120981.text: All -amino acids have a general formula R - CH ( NH ₂)- COOH (except proline). If the side chain R is - CH ₂- COOH , identify the correct name and the nature of the amino acid.
120981.sol: The given side chain is R = - CH ₂- COOH . Substituting this into the general formula R - CH ( NH ₂)- COOH gives the structure of Aspartic acid. Because the molecule contains two carboxyl ( - COOH ) groups and only one amino ( - NH ₂ ) group, it has more acidic groups than basic groups. Therefore, it is classified as an acidic amino acid. Glutamic acid has the side chain - CH ₂- CH ₂- COOH . Asparagine has the side chain - CH ₂- CONH ₂ and is neutral. Answer: Aspartic acid, Acidic

121828.subject: Botany
121828.text: What important evolutionary step is indicated by the development of zygotes within the female gametophytes?
121828.sol: Zygote thereafter produces a multicellular well-differentiated sporophyte which is the dominant phase of the pteridophytes. In the majority of the pteridophytes all the spores are of similar kinds; such plants are called homosporous. Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores, are known as heterosporous. The megaspores and microspores germinate and give rise to female and male gametophytes, respectively. The female gametophytes in these plants are

122378.subject: Botany
122378.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Mantle cavity in molluscs is significant for their life functions Reason: A soft and spongy layer of skin forms a mantle over the visceral hump.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
122378.sol: Mantle cavity in molluscs is significant for their life functions as the cavity contains feather like gills which help in excretion and respiration.

122396.subject: Botany
122396.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Phylum Mollusca is the largest animal phylum Reason: This phylum consists of all the insects
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
122396.sol: Phylum Mollusca is the second largest animal phylum. Molluscs are terrestrial or aquatic having an organ-system level of organisation.

122594.subject: Botany
122594.text: Which of the following sets of characteristics is unique to Class Aves?
options: Feathers, pneumatic bones and forelimbs modified into wings
122594.sol: According to NCERT, the characteristic features of Aves (birds) are the presence of feathers and forelimbs modified into wings. Their endoskeleton is fully ossified (bony) and the long bones are hollow with air cavities (pneumatic). Pinna is a unique mammalian character, not found in birds. Birds have a completely four-chambered heart, making the option with a three-chambered heart incorrect. Birds possess pneumatic bones, not solid bones, which helps in reducing their body weight for flight. Answer: Feathers, pneu

123156.subject: Botany
123156.text: Coconut's husk fibre, coir of commerce is extracted from
123156.sol: Commercial coir is obtained from the fibrous husk (mesocarp) of fruits of coconut palm. The fibre is valued for its lightness and exceedingly high resistance to mechanical wear and dampness.

123558.subject: Botany
123558.text: What phase of the cell cycle corresponds to the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication?
123558.sol: G1 phase corresponds to the interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication. During the G1 phase the cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA. S or synthesis phase marks the period during which DNA synthesis or replication takes place. During this time the amount of DNA per cell doubles. If the initial amount of DNA is denoted as 2C then it increases to 4C. However, there is no increase in the chromosome number; if the cell had diploid or 2n number of chromosomes

123856.subject: Botany
123856.text: Match List I with List II: List I List II A. Leptotene I. Recombination nodules appear B. Zygotene II. X-shaped structures become visible C. Pachytene III. Compaction of chromosomes continues D. Diplotene IV. Bivalents are formed E. Diakinesis V. Assembly of meiotic spindle begins Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
123856.sol: The correct matching of the sub-stages of Prophase I with their defining events is as follows: Leptotene: Compaction of chromosomes continues throughout this stage. Zygotene: Homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) and bivalents are formed. Pachytene: Recombination nodules appear and crossing over occurs. Diplotene: Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex occurs and X-shaped structures called chiasmata become visible. Diakinesis: The meiotic spindle is assembled to prepare the homologous chromosomes for separatio

123942.subject: Botany
123942.text: Polyploidy can be induced by the application of
123942.sol: Colchicine is a poisonous chemical, isolated from seeds and bulbs of autumn crocus (Colchicum autumnale). It blocks spindle formation and thus, inhibits the movement of sister chromatids to the opposite poles. The resulting restitution nucleus includes all the chromatids. As a result, the chromosome number of the cell is doubled, which leads to polyploidy.

124240.subject: Botany
124240.text: Chromatin Components Types of Proteins A. Histones 1. Basic proteins aiding in DNA packaging B. Non-Histone Proteins 2. Part of chromatin and involved in various functions C. RNA 3. Genetic material distributed among chromosomes D. DNA 4. Nucleic acid involved in various functions within chromatin
124240.sol: Histones are basic proteins aiding in DNA packaging.Non-histone proteins are involved in various functions within chromatin.DNA is the genetic material distributed among chromosomes.RNA is a nucleic acid involved in various functions within chromatin.

124465.subject: Botany
124465.text: Cell membrane in animals is composed mainly of the molecule of :
124465.sol: Chemically, the plasma membrane or cell membrane is made up of 60 % proteins and 40 % lipids. The percentage of carbohydrates ranges from 1-10 which are in the form of glycoproteins or glycolipids. Proteins may be extrinsic (peripheral) and intrinsic (integral) while lipids may be phospholipids, glycolipids and sterols.

125073.subject: Botany
125073.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The process of fermentation are hazardous - either acid or alcohol is produced. Reason: Yeasts poison themselves to death when the concentration of alcohol reaches 50 per cent.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
125073.sol: The process of fermentation are hazardous - either acid or alcohol is produced. Yeasts poison themselves to death when the concentration of alcohol reaches 13 per cent.

125432.subject: Botany
125432.text: What is the end product of the reduction phase in the Calvin cycle?
125432.sol: These are a series of reactions that lead to the formation of glucose. The steps involve utilisation of 2 molecules of ATP for phosphorylation and two of NADPH for reduction per CO2 molecule fixed. The fixation of six molecules of CO2 and 6 turns of the cycle are required for the formation of one molecule of glucose from the pathway. Regeneration of the CO2 acceptor molecule RuBP is crucial if the cycle is to continue uninterrupted. The regeneration steps require one ATP for phosphorylation to form RuBP.

125892.subject: Botany
125892.text: How do Vallisneria flowers achieve pollination?
options: By emerging above water and attracting insects
By being carried passively by water currents
By using sticky pollen to adhere to water
125892.sol: Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants and is limited to about 30 genera, mostly monocotyledons. As against this, you would recall that water is a regular mode of transport for the male gametes among the lower plant groups such as algae, bryophytes and pteridophytes. It is believed, particularly for some bryophytes and pteridophytes, that their distribution is limited because of the need for water for the transport of male gametes and fertilisation. Some examples of water pollinated plants are Valli

126811.subject: Botany
126811.text: Malonate inhibits the growth of pathogenic bacteria by inhibiting the activity of:
126811.sol: The activity of any enzyme is extremely sensitive to the presence of specific chemicals that bind to the enzyme. Inhibitors are capable of switching off the activity of enzyme. When the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme, it is known as competitive inhibitor . Competitive inhibitors compete with the substrate for the substrate binding site of the enzyme and block the activity. The inhibition of succinic dehydrogenase enzyme by malonate which

If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.

127151.subject: Botany
127151.text: How many plant species might there be yet to be discovered and described in India?
127151.sol: Although India has only 2.4 per cent of the world’s land area, its share of the global species diversity is an impressive 8.1 per cent. That is what makes our country one of the 12 mega diversity countries of the world. Nearly 45,000 species of plants and twice as many of animals have been recorded from India. How many living species are actually there waiting to be discovered and named? If we accept May’s global estimates, only 22 per cent of the total species have been recorded so far. Applying this proportion to

127434.subject: Botany
127434.text: Tropical regions show greatest level of species richness because A. Tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years, hence more time was available for species diversification. B. Tropical environments are more seasonal. C. More solar energy is available in tropics. D. Constant environments promote niche specialization. E. Tropical environments are constant and predictable. Choose the cor
options: A, C, D and E only
127434.sol: Only statement B is incorrect because tropical environments unlike temperate ones, are less seasonal, relatively more constant and predictable. Thus statements A , C , D and E are correct.

127745.subject: Botany
127745.text: Common detritivores in our ecosystem are___.
127745.sol: Common detritivores in our ecosystem are earthworms.

Statement (II) is correct: The ciliated epithelium is primarily located in the inner lining of hollow organs such as bronchioles and fallopian tubes to move particles or mucus in a specific direction. Statement (III) is correct: Glandular epithelium is formed when some of the columnar or cuboidal cells become specialised for secretion. Statement (IV) is correct: Unice

129204.subject: Zoology
129204.text: What is the inner surface of the axonal membrane of a resting neuron charged with?
129204.sol: The electrical potential difference across the resting plasma membrane is called the resting potential. The outer surface of the axonal membrane possesses a positive charge while its inner surface becomes negatively charged and therefore is polarised. The membrane of a neuron is polarised due to the presence of different types of ion channels and the ionic gradients maintained by the sodium-potassium pump. The fluid outside the axon in a resting state contains a low concentration of K⁺, a high concentration of Na⁺

129384.subject: Zoology
129384.text: Assertion : The optic nerves leave the eye at the point called blind spot. Reason: Only cone are densely packed at the blind spot, hence is the name.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
129384.sol: The nerve fibres from all parts of the retina converge to leave through a point called blindspot. It is the place in the visual field that corresponds to the lack of light detecting photo receptor cells on the optic disc of the retina.

129679.subject: Zoology
129679.text: Select the components eliminated by Sebaceous glands.
129679.sol: Sebaceous glands are responsible to eliminate certain substances like sterols, hydrocarbons and waxes through sebum.

129702.subject: Zoology

List I List II (A) Renin (I) Powerful vasoconstrictor (B) Angiotensin II (II) Causes vasodilation and decreases blood pressure (C) Aldosterone (III) Released by JG cells (D) Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) (IV) Causes reabsorption of Na ⁺ and water from distal parts of tubule Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
129702.sol: Renin is an enzyme released by the juxtaglomerular (JG) cells in response to a fall in glomerular blood pressure. Angiotensin II is a powerful vasoconstrictor that increases glomerular blood pressure. Aldosterone is a hormone from the adrenal cortex that causes the reabsorption of Na ⁺ and water from the distal parts of the tubule. 129829.subject: Zoology
129829.text: What is the purpose of clinical assessment of pulmonary functions?
options: To measure the volume of air involved in breathing movements
To determine the strength of inspiration and expiration
To evaluate the functioning of the lungs
129829.sol: Similarly, expiration takes place when the intra-pulmonary pressure is higher than the atmospheric pressure. The diaphragm and a specialised set of muscles – external and internal intercostals between the ribs, help in generation of such gradients. Inspiration is initiated by the contraction of diaphragm which increases the volume of thoracic chamber in the antero-posterior axis. The contraction of external inter-costal muscles lifts up the ribs and the sternum causing an increase in the volume of the thoracic cham

130022.subject: Zoology
130022.text: Hemoglobin Form Oxygen-Binding Capacity A. Carboxyhemoglobin 1. Bound with CO2 B. Deoxyhemoglobin 2. No oxygen bound C. Carbaminohemoglobin 3. Bound with CO (carbon monoxide) D. Oxyhemoglobin 4. Fully saturated with oxygen
130022.sol: Carboxyhemoglobin is bound with CO (carbon monoxide). Deoxyhemoglobin has no oxygen bound to it. Carbaminohemoglobin is bound with CO2. Oxyhemoglobin is fully saturated with oxygen.

130028.subject: Zoology

130028.sol: Trachea is the site of gaseous exchange in an insect.

130076.subject: Zoology
130076.text: Identify the correct name and the standard average value of the volume of air that will remain in the lungs after a normal expiration in a healthy human.
130076.sol: The volume of air that remains in the lungs after a normal expiration is called the Functional Residual Capacity (FRC). It includes the Expiratory Reserve Volume (ERV) and the Residual Volume (RV). FRC = ERV + RV According to standard physiological values in a healthy human: ERV = 1000 - 1100 mL RV = 1100 - 1200 mL Therefore, FRC = (1000 + 1100) to (1100 + 1200) mL = 2100 - 2300 mL. Residual Volume ( 1100 - 1200 mL) is the air remaining after a forcible expiration. Expiratory Capacity ( 1500 - 1600 mL) is the total

130286.subject: Zoology
130286.text: Which type of joint allows considerable movement?
130286.sol: Joints are essential for all types of movements involving the bony parts of the body. Locomotory movements are no exception to this. Force generated by the muscles is used to carry out movement through joints. Synovial joints are characterised by the presence of a fluid-filled synovial cavity between the articulating surfaces of the two bones. Such an arrangement allows considerable movement. The flat skull bones fuse end-to-end with the help of dense fibrous connective tissues in the form of sutures, to form the c

130317.subject: Zoology
130317.text: Match the following with the help of diagram: Name of the bone Number of bones in body Cervical a) 5 Thoracic b) 7 Lumbar c) 1 Sacral d) 12
130317.sol: Our vertebral column is formed by 26 serially arranged units called vertebrae and is dorsally placed. It extends from the base of the skull and constitutes the main framework of the trunk. Each vertebra has a central hollow portion (neural canal) through which the spinal cord passes. First vertebra is the atlas and it articulates with the occipital condyles. The vertebral column is differentiated into cervical (7), thoracic (12), lumbar (5), sacral (1-fused) and coccygeal (1-fused) regions starting from the skull.

Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
131064.sol: Placenta acts as an endocrine tissue and produces several hormones like human chorionic gonadotrophin, human placental lactogen, estrogens, progestogens,etc.

(iii) The total number of genes is estimated at 30,000–much lower than previous estimates of 80,000 to 1,40,000 genes. Almost all (99.9 per cent) nucleotide bases are exactly the same in all people. 132449.subject: Zoology
132449.text: Which of the following Mendelian disorders is inherited as a sex-linked recessive trait?
132449.sol: Colour blindness is a sex-linked (X-linked) recessive trait. Cystic fibrosis, phenylketonuria, and thalassemia are all inherited as autosomal recessive traits. Students often confuse thalassemia with sex-linked blood disorders like haemophilia, but thalassemia is strictly autosomal. Answer: Colour blindness

The substances to which such an immune response is produced are called allergens. The antibodies produced to these are of IgE type. Common examples of allergens are mites in dust, pollens, animal dander, etc. Symptoms of allergic reactions include sneezing, watery eyes, running nose and difficulty in breathing. 133623.subject: Zoology
133623.text: Which of the following sets includes all bacterial disease?
133623.sol: Diptheria, leprosy and plague are the bacterial diseases of humans. Diptheria is a serious airborne contagious disease. It is caused by Cornybacterium diptheriae which is a Grampositive bacterium. It is inhaled through droplets and reaches to respiratory tract and infects it. Leprosy or Hansen's disease is a contact disease, caused by bacterium Mycobacterium leprae. It degenerates the tissues and deforms the body organs. Plague is a disease caused by bacterium Yersinia pestis or Pasteurella pestis.

134043.subject: Zoology
134043.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
134043.text: Assertion : Inbreeding produces pureline. Reason : It causes homozygosity.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
134043.sol: Inbreeding refers to the mating of closely related individuals within the same breed for 46 generations. Superior males and superior females of the same breed are identified and mated in pairs. The progeny obtained from such matings are evaluated and superior males and females among them are identified for further mating. Inbreeding increases homozygosity. Thus inbreeding is necessary if we want to evolve a pureline in any animal.

A single DNA sequence coding for intact human proinsulin

134313.sol: In 1983, Eli Lilly prepared two DNA sequences corresponding to the A and B chains of human insulin and introduced them into plasmids of Escherichia coli to produce insulin chains. A single DNA sequence for proinsulin was not used because bacteria lack the enzymes required to remove the C-peptide and process proinsulin into mature insulin. 135161.text: What does brood parasitism in birds involve?
options: A bird laying eggs in another bird’s nest
A bird feeding on another bird’s eggs
A bird living within another bird’s nest
A bird incubating its own eggs in a different nest
135161.sol: Brood parasitism in birds is a fascinating example of parasitism in which the parasitic bird lays its eggs in the nest of its host and lets the host incubate them. During the course of evolution, the eggs of the parasitic bird have evolved to resemble the host’s egg in size and color to reduce the chances of the host bird detecting the foreign eggs and ejecting them from the nest. options: Establishing sacred groves in forest areas
Cryopreservation of gametes in liquid nitrogen

6a16f3287cfacf7984f86722.sol: Conservation strategies are broadly classified into in-situ (on-site) and ex-situ (off-site) conservation. 95200.subject: Botany
95200.text: Consider the following statements and choose the correct option. 1. The thread-like cytoplasmic strands, running from one cell to other is known as plasmodesmata. 2. Xylem and phloem constitute the vascular bundle of the stem. 3. The first formed xylem elements are described as metaxylem. 4. Radial vascular bundles are mainly found in the leaves.
options: II is true, but I, III and IV are false
III is true, but I, II and IV are false
IV is true, but I, II and III are false
I and II are true, but III and IV are false
95200.sol: Plasmodesmata are thread-like cytoplasmic strands running from one cell to other and these make connections between adjacent cells. Each vascular bundle is made up necessarily of xylem and phloem elements and the cambium may or may not be present. The first differentiated xylem is called protoxylem, whereas those differentiated afterward are called metaxylem. Radial vascular bundles are mainly found in the roots. In these, there are separate and alternate strands of phloem and xylem present on different radii.

96687.subject: Botany
96687.text: Which one of the following is not a micronutrient?
96687.sol: Magnesium is a macronutrient. Micronutrients are essential elements that are required by plants in a small amount. They include Fe, Cu, B, Mo, Mn, Cl, and Ni. Macronutrients, on the other hand, are those essential elements that are required by plants in a larger amount. The examples include C, H, 0, N, S, P, K, Ca, and Mg.

Stigma is the tip of carpel and is the receptive surface for pollen grains.
96899.sol: Sepals are green leaf like like structure which protects the flower in bud condition, if green they also carry out photosynthesis. Petals if brightly coloured attracts insects for pollination. Staminodes are sterile stamen which does not produces pollen grains.

304488.subject: Physics
304488.text: Which of the following sets of physical quantities cannot be taken as fundamental quantities in any system of units?
304488.sol: Fundamental quantities in any system of units must be independent of each other, meaning no quantity in the set can be derived from the other quantities in the same set. In the set containing length, time and velocity, velocity can be expressed as the ratio of length to time ( v = L T ). Since velocity is not independent of length and time, this set cannot be chosen as a set of fundamental quantities. In all other given sets, the three quantities are mutually independent.
